subject: SOC 2 evidence & cloud carve-out clarification — PulseHealth onboarding
content:
From: Elena Morales <emorales@pulsehealth.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 evidence & cloud carve-out clarification — PulseHealth onboarding

Hi Kimberly / Marissa,

We're kicking off vendor onboarding for Redwood and need to collect SOC 2 documentation and carve-out clarifications for our security team. A few specific asks to help us close our assessment quickly:

1) SOC 2 Type II report (most recent) and date range for the audit period.
2) Any bridge letter or attestation that references carve-outs for cloud providers (AWS/GCP) and whether Redwood relies on provider SOC reports for specific controls.
3) A current subprocessor inventory (name, role, region, contract link or PO reference) and whether subprocessors have access to customer data or logs.
4) Confirmation of key custody model: does Redwood manage encryption keys (KMS customer-managed or Redwood-managed keys)?
5) Specifics on backups/snapshots and where those are stored (S3, EBS snapshots, region) and whether those are included/excluded from Redwood's SOC scope.

Our audit window is coming up; if you can provide the items above or a plan and timeline we can put an assessment slot on May 1 for the security review.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if it helps.

Elena Morales
Security Operations Manager
PulseHealth
security@pulsehealth.com

-----Original Message-----
On Fri, 9 Apr 2027 at 09:18 AM kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai> wrote:

> From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
> To: Elena Morales <emorales@pulsehealth.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
> Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
> Subject: Re: SOC 2 evidence & cloud carve-out clarification — PulseHealth onboarding
>
> Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. We're able to provide the SOC 2 Type II report and a subprocessor inventory right away, and we can draft an AWS carve-out bridge letter that explains how we map controls to the cloud provider's SOC.
>
> Quick notes up front so expectations are aligned: Redwood operates on AWS for production, and many infrastructure-level controls (physical data center, certain networking controls, underlying hypervisor) are covered by AWS SOC reports. For customer data custody and encryption keys: by default Redwood manages KMS keys on behalf of customers (Redwood-managed KMS) for hosted deployments; Dedicated/Private customers can request customer-managed KMS — we note that in contracts.
>
> Action items / proposed timeline:
> - Attach: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026.pdf (stub) — full Type II report (redacted where required).
> - Attach: subprocessors_list_20270409.csv (stub) — current inventory with access notes.
> - Draft bridge letter for AWS carve-out: we can share a preliminary letter by EOD Tue 2027-04-12. The letter will: describe the shared-responsibility mapping, note which infrastructure controls we rely on AWS for, and call out services excluded from Redwood's audit scope (e.g., underlying hypervisor, AWS-managed services for which we rely on provider reports).
> - Confirm backups/snapshots: I'll loop in Jonas to confirm exactly which snapshot types are included in our scope and whether any archival snapshots are managed by Redwood or by AWS.
>
> Would a 30-minute call on Mon 2027-04-12 10:00 PT work to walk through the bridge letter language and the subprocessor inventory?
>
> Best,
>
> Kimberly Park
> Senior Security & Compliance Manager
> Redwood Inference
> attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026.pdf (stub), subprocessors_list_20270409.csv (stub)

Please call out: which AWS SOC sections we rely on, and explicitly name any AWS services we carve out (EBS snapshots, underlying DR/physical controls). Also confirm whether our snapshot retention for hosted customers includes cross-region copies that might be treated differently for compliance.
>
> Jonas: Tim in Infra also needs to confirm whether KMS keys for the PulseHealth tenant (they signed for hosted) are Redwood-managed or can be converted to customer-managed ahead of onboarding. If we can offer customer-managed KMS for their production tenant that should be called out.
>

>
> - Audit window our team needs to validate against: 2026-05-01 to 2026-10-31. Please confirm the Redwood Type II report covers (or maps to) that period or provide a bridge letter covering the gap.
> - For carve-outs: we need the bridge letter to explicitly call out EBS snapshots and S3 backups as "covered by AWS SOC" where applicable, and to state whether Redwood retains admin access to snapshot metadata/logs.
> - Attached our vendor evidence intake form (PulseHealth_vendor_evidence_form.pdf) — fill the form fields where possible and return with your artifacts.
>
> If you can send the SOC 2 report and subprocessor inventory now and the bridge letter draft by Tue 4/12, we'll slot the technical review on May 1. Call on Mon 4/12 10:00 PT is good — marissa, can you send a calendar invite?
